transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (StellarPay Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Platform), Hannah Ortiz (Security), Dave (PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick call today, POC weekly sync focusing on onboarding and environment readiness.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Yep, thanks Maya. We're hoping to get the staging env ready so we can run the load test next week.
[00:13] Marcus Lee: I can give a quick update from infra side. We've created a staging VPC but still need to decide on bastion vs direct peering, and we need Redwood to confirm the required ports and IP CIDRs.
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: Great, Marcus. On our side we need the bastion jump host details and the egress rules for outbound so the runtime can call out for model pulls if using hosted variants. If you're doing private deployment, we'll need the KMS endpoint and certs.
[00:35] Hannah Ortiz: From security, two things: SOC 2 docs and pen test summary; also we have to validate KMS/HSM flow. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS?
[00:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated options. For hosted we offer envelope encryption but we can integrate with your KMS for the Private deployment. I'll send the exact integration notes.
[00:55] Dave (PM): Timeline wise, we want the noisy early validation by end of next week. If we can do a short load today that'd be ideal — but I know access is the blocker.
[01:05] Priya Nair: We also need to validate quality regressed after quantization—so part of the acceptance criteria is model output match within a threshold.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Understood. We'll include model/quantization profiles in the benchmark runbook. I'll also add a step for golden prompt validation and automated evals.
[01:20] Marcus Lee: Status update: firewall team needs a list of source IPs to whitelist for the redwood test runs. I can open a small range but prefer using a bastion.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Fair. We can also do an SSH jump approach — we'll send a recommended minimal CIDR and the ports (SSH 22, HTTPS 443) and any ephemeral ports for metrics ingestion.
[01:40] Hannah Ortiz: Also SSO — we want to lock down console access. Does Redwood Console support SAML/SSO provisioning?
[01:47] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML SSO is supported; we can share the metadata and the on-boarding steps. For the POC we can do account-level creds but recommend SSO for production.
[01:58] Priya Nair: Quick question, for the POC are we using Redwood Hosted models or are we testing a dedicated/private deployment? That affects KMS and network flow.
[02:07] Maya Chen: For this POC we proposed dedicated capacity in staging to replicate your latency profile, but we can fall back to hosted if needed. Dedicated will give you predictable throughput and isolated data handling.
[02:16] Priya Nair: Ok dedicated makes sense; just need to know the costs and any limitations around plugins or tool-calling.
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: Tool calling works; we support function calling and structured outputs. For dedicated we can recommend quantization profiles to save cost, but we'll show regression numbers in the benchmark.
[02:33] Dave (PM): On cost, can you provide a rough delta between hosted vs dedicated for our expected load?
[02:39] Maya Chen: We'll follow up with a cost estimate based on the profiling data you already shared. I'll include unit cost and rough monthly projection for the pilot.
[02:47] Marcus Lee: About the data transfer — our PCI team flagged egress monitoring. Is there an audit trail or per-request logging that we can ship to our SIEM?
[02:56] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we produce audit logs and request traces that can be exported; we can also push logs to your S3 or Splunk depending on the integration. We'll share the schema for the audit logs.
[03:08] Hannah Ortiz: Can you confirm log retention defaults and encryption at rest?
[03:14] Maya Chen: Default is 90 days for POC but we can configure retention. All logs at rest are encrypted; if you want customer-managed keys for logs we can discuss.
[03:23] Priya Nair: Marcus, do you have an ETA on the bastion?
[03:26] Marcus Lee: I can get the bastion stood up by Wednesday, 2025-06-18, but need the CIDR ranges from Redwood and the credentials format.
[03:35] Maya Chen: I'll email the CIDR list and the recommended SSH key format after the call.
[03:40] Dave (PM): For the runbook — what will the benchmark include? Latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost, and quality checks?
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: Exactly. We'll measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, throughput under request patterns, and run the golden prompt suite for quality regression. We'll also record per-token cost and provide suggestions for batching/caching and quantization.
[04:02] Priya Nair: About the golden prompts — I'll upload a canonical set of 200 prompts and expected answers. We need an automated diff and fidelity metric.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: We'll wire up an automated eval that calculates BLEU/ROUGE-ish scores and a custom semantic similarity metric; note sometimes transcriptions in the eval can be noisy so we'll do human sampling too.
[04:22] Hannah Ortiz: Any compliance artifacts you can share now?
[04:25] Maya Chen: I'll send SOC 2 Type II, the pen test executive summary, and the data flow diagram. Also a short note on KMS integration patterns (customer KMS for private).
[04:35] Marcus Lee: Also, what's the plan for model versions? Can we pin a model during the POC so inference is reproducible?
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can pin a model version and we support rollbacks and canary routing. For the benchmark we'll pin the same version across runs.
[04:50] Priya Nair: One more question: are there any constraints around sequence length for the quantized variants? We saw weird tokens being dropped in early tests.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: Good call — quantized runtimes sometimes have sequence-length tradeoffs. We'll include checks for max context and KV cache behavior; sometimes it's a kernel selection issue and we can tweak.
[05:09] Maya Chen: Ok looks like we have the key blockers: access to bastion/VPC, Marcus to provide the CIDR/jump host; Redwood to send security pack; Liam to prepare benchmark runbook.
[05:18] Dave (PM): Agree. Can we target the load test for Tuesday 2025-06-24?
[05:23] Marcus Lee: Tentative yes, pending access.
[05:26] Priya Nair: We also want an interim smoke test as soon as the bastion is up — just to verify connectivity and a single inference path.
[05:34] Maya Chen: We'll plan a smoke test day-of-bastion — Liam will run a quick smoke, then the full load the following week.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: I'll post the runbook in the shared drive and leave notes for the infra team.
[05:45] Hannah Ortiz: For the SSO onboarding, do you have a doc?
[05:49] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML SSO doc will be part of the security pack.
[05:53] Dave (PM): Any other blockers?
[05:56] Priya Nair: Not on my side.
[05:58] Marcus Lee: No. I'll start the bastion and share creds to the SRE channel.
[06:02] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items discussed. Recap of next steps in email.
[06:07] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Bye.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: some product names may be mis-heard in the meeting (eg "Red wood" or "KV cash"), timestamps are approximate, speaker labels taken from calendar but may not map exactly to the voice in automated transcript.
